provenance: Model-knowledge snapshot, NOT a live feed. Verify against the issuer's current terms before presenting a rate as fact.
notes: The UK cashback market is far thinner than the US one. Most cards pay well under 1% and several use annual-spend tiers that this engine flattens to a single base rate; the per-card notes flag where that happens. Section 75 protection and no-FX-fee status are often worth more to a UK cardholder than the headline cashback rate.

cards.name: American Express Cashback Everyday (UK)
cards.base_label: 0.5% on the first £10,000 of annual spend
cards.notes: Rate rises to 1% on annual spend above £10,000, and a 5% introductory rate applies for the first few months within a cap. Cashback is only paid once a year and only above a minimum threshold. Amex acceptance is materially worse than Visa/Mastercard in UK supermarkets and small retailers.

cards.name: American Express Platinum Cashback (UK)
cards.base_label: 0.75% on the first £10,000 of annual spend
cards.notes: Rate rises to 1.25% above £10,000 of annual spend. Only worth the annual fee at fairly high spend; run the break-even before recommending it over the free version.

cards.name: American Express Nectar (UK)

rules.label: 3 Nectar points per £1 at Nectar partners
rules.note: Partner earning depends on linking the Nectar account correctly; verify the current partner list.

cards.notes: Nectar points are worth roughly 0.5p each at standard redemption, so 2 points per £1 is about 1% - higher only if the user reliably uses Nectar boosted redemptions.

cards.name: Barclaycard Rewards
cards.notes: The real draw is no foreign transaction fee and no cash withdrawal fee abroad, not the 0.25% rate. For any purchase in a foreign currency this usually beats a 1% cashback card that charges a 3% FX fee.

rules.label: 2% on supermarket and travel spend in the first year
rules.note: Introductory-period rate with a monthly cashback cap and a monthly fee. Verify whether the user is still inside the promotional period.

cards.name: John Lewis Partnership Credit Card

rules.label: 1 point per £1 at John Lewis and Waitrose

cards.notes: Points convert to John Lewis and Waitrose vouchers only, so they are worth face value to a regular John Lewis shopper and nothing to anyone else.
